status_summary: No program named or modeled as a clean standards initiative was found. America's AI Action Plan, released 2025-07-23, recommends that State and Commerce use U.S. influence in diplomatic and standard-setting bodies to promote innovation-friendly AI governance and counter authoritarian influence. A presidential memorandum of 2025-12-19, Winning the 6G Race, states a policy of advancing U.S. interests in international standards bodies and directs the Secretary of State to build a coalition of industry and foreign partners for the 2027 World Radiocommunication Conference, without naming China or any vendor. On 2026-07-27 NTIA launched a non-binding Call to Action for 6G Leadership and Security, endorsed by 25 governments, under which participants intend to coordinate with industry on global 6G standards and strong security standards; like the memorandum, it names no country or vendor and is narrower than the comprehensive standards initiative the chapter describes.

timeline.event: The White House released America's AI Action Plan, which recommends that State and Commerce use U.S. influence in diplomatic and standard-setting bodies to promote innovation-friendly AI governance and counter authoritarian influence.

A presidential memorandum, Winning the 6G Race, set a policy of advancing U.S. interests in international standards bodies for 6G, directed NTIA spectrum studies, and directed the Secretary of State to build a coalition of industry and foreign partners for the 2027 World Radiocommunication Conference.

NTIA launched the Call to Action for 6G Leadership and Security, endorsed by 25 governments; participants intend to coordinate with industry on global 6G standards and security baselines, with milestones over 12 months. The text is non-binding and names no country or vendor.

title: Launch a clean standards initiative to counter CCP influence over technology standards
uncertainties: Five searches were run in research on this item (State, Commerce and NIST standards actions; the State Department plan; FY2026 defense authorization provisions; a 6G initiative; the 6G call text), and one more in review located the December 2025 memorandum on whitehouse.gov. The NTIA press page cites the memorandum and mentions neither standards nor China; only the call document addresses standards, and the call is dated by the press release because the PDF prints no date. The press release says more than 20 partner governments while the call lists 25 endorsers; the record uses the call's figure. The memorandum's NSPM number is inferred from its web address and is not printed in its text. The Action Plan PDF prints only July 2025; the 2025-07-23 release date comes from a law-firm tracker dated that day, and the Action Plan was not re-opened in review. The State Department 2026-2030 plan could not be opened; its standards language comes from one trade article and is not counted as an event. A CRS note on cyber and AI provisions of the FY2026 defense authorization law showed no standards provision, but the full law was not searched. No NIST Federal Register notice on China and standards was found. The record's agency field follows the chapter (FCC), but the actions found are by NTIA, the State Department and the White House; no FCC standards initiative was found. The stage is a judgment: the Action Plan item is a recommendation, the memorandum's standards language is a general policy statement, and the 6G call is a voluntary statement of intent that does not target CCP influence, so proposed 15 with a partial match is used; in_progress 25 is defensible if the 6G call is read as the launch of an allied standards effort.
